A.explanation: Efficiency is a ratio of two energies or two powers, so the units cancel and it has no unit.

B.explanation: The joule $\text{J}$ is the unit of energy and work, not of the ratio useful energy divided by input energy.

C.explanation: The metre $\text{m}$ is the unit of distance, which does not appear as the unit of the efficiency ratio.

D.explanation: The watt $\text{W}$ is the unit of power, not of the ratio useful power divided by input power.

hints: Recall how efficiency is defined from useful output and total input energy or power in this question.
Write the ratio $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output} / \text{total input}$ and check what units the top and bottom have.
If top and bottom are both in joules or both in watts, decide what happens to the unit when you divide them.
walkthrough: Identify the definition: $\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{\text{useful energy output}}{\text{total energy input}} = \dfrac{\text{useful power output}}{\text{total power input}}$.
Note the units: energy output and input are both in joules $\text{J}$, and power output and input are both in watts $\text{W}$.
Divide the units: $\text{J}/\text{J} = 1$ or $\text{W}/\text{W} = 1$, so the units cancel and efficiency is dimensionless.
This means efficiency is often given as a decimal or a percentage, with no SI base unit attached.
Joule, metre and watt therefore describe other quantities, not efficiency. This is option A.
